subject: Reconcile streaming vs embeddings usage—unexpected overage
messages:
From: Maria Rossi <maria.rossi@acropolis.ai>
To: Acropolis Billing <billing@acropolis.ai>, aditya.rao@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 1 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected July invoice — streaming vs embeddings charges

Hi team,

We're reviewing our July invoice (INV-ACR-0727) and see a ~3.2x spike in token charges compared to our forecast. We only increased streaming usage for a new feature in mid-July, but embeddings volume stayed flat. The invoice line items show large streaming token counts and a matching VAT charge; we need a breakdown and the raw usage export for audit.

Specific asks:
- CSV export of per-request token counts for 2027-07-01 to 2027-07-31 (with timestamps and request IDs)
- Clarify whether streamed partial responses or retries are double-counted in metering
- Confirm VAT treatment for our EU entity (we provided a UK VAT id last quarter)

Can you put the invoice on hold until we reconcile? We're prepared to pay the baseline for known usage but want to pause collection on the contested amount.

Thanks,
Maria Rossi
Head of Finance | Acropolis AI
maria.rossi@acropolis.ai
+44 20 7946 0123

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: aditya.rao@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Investigate streaming token delta for Acropolis (sample attached)

Aditya / Karthik — attaching the small sample and a quick debug dump from the runtime. Initial read: when clients use streaming with incremental flushes, our metering treats each flush boundary as continuing the same completion but still counts generated tokens; however, there was a corner-case where a retry of the final chunk (client-side reconnect within 30s) caused the server to replay the last 1–2 chunks and they were not deduplicated in the metering index because the request-id changed on reconnect. That explains duplicate counts for long-running streams that had transient disconnects.

Evidence: see redwood_tokenization_debug.log (included) — you can correlate request_id 20270801-ACR-RT-99 with duplicated token groups at 2027-07-18T14:02:05Z and 2027-07-18T14:02:12Z. In the export I filtered to only keep the earliest occurrence per session_id which reduces billed tokens by ~38% for the affected window.

Mitigation:
- Immediate: apply a one-time adjustment for duplicated tokens in July for affected request_ids (I can produce the exact credit delta).
- Short-term: we'll push a metering dedupe patch to the runtime that matches reconnects within the 60s window by client session id rather than request id.
- Long-term: add a webhook export so customers can ingest raw events for reconciliation in near-real-time.

I'll prepare the per-request CSV and the list of request_ids impacted; please confirm you want us to proceed with the adjustment and invoice credit.

— Priyom
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai

Attachment: redwood_tokenization_debug.log (text)
From: aditya.rao@redwood.ai <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Maria Rossi <maria.rossi@acropolis.ai>
Cc: billing@redwood.ai, priyom.das@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected July invoice — streaming vs embeddings charges

Hi Maria — quick update and proposed resolution. Thanks for your patience while we investigated.

Summary of findings:
- Root cause: short reconnects during streaming completions caused duplicated final chunks to be billed because the metering key used request_id rather than session_id.
- Impact: ~36.9% of the contested streaming token charges on July invoice attributable to duplicated chunks across ~1.7k requests (sampled and verified against your payloads).
- VAT: we confirmed your supplied VAT ID (GB999999971) is on file for Acropolis AI Ltd and the July invoice will be updated to reflect reverse-charge treatment where applicable.

What we did / will do now:
1) Applied an invoice hold on the contested amount and issued a provisional credit of EUR 12,320.45 while we finalize exact bookkeeping (you should see a proforma credit notice attached to the invoice).
2) Attached per-request CSV export (shared via Drive link) with request IDs, timestamps, original billed tokens, and adjusted token counts. See: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_link
3) Engineering will deploy a dedupe patch to the metering service by Fri 2027-08-06 UTC and backfill corrected counts for July.
4) Finance will reissue the corrected invoice and VAT reconciliation within 5 business days.

Please confirm:
- That the provisional credit amount is acceptable to Acropolis (we can make it final after you confirm the per-request file).
- Whether you want us to enable the near-real-time webhook export for your account; this will give you a live stream of metering events for reconciliation.

Again, apologies for the disruption — we appreciate the catch. If you prefer a short call to walk through the CSV I can set one up with Priyom and Karthik.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0128
